message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need to know | |---------|-----------------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are tallied from the cards left in opponents’ hands when you finish a round. | | **Players** | 2–10 (standard deck works best with 4–8). | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”, two “Draw Two”) + 4 “Wild” + 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two”, the first player draws two and loses a turn). | | **Turn Order** | Players sit in a circle. The first player is the one to the left of the dealer. Turn order moves clockwise unless a “Reverse” card changes direction. | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either the color or the number/symbol of the top card on the discard pile. If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | 1. **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
2. **Reverse** – Changes play direction.
3. **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
4. **Wild** – You choose the new color.
5. **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise, you can be challenged.) | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player calls you out before the next turn starts, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all of their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbered cards = face value, Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points each, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points each. | | **Winning the Game** | First player to reach 500 points (or your chosen target) wins. If you’re playing a single round, the highest scorer wins that round. | | **House Variations** | • **Draw‑Four Challenge** – If you suspect a player illegally played a Wild Draw Four, they can challenge. If the challenger is right, the player who played the card draws 4 cards instead of the challenger. If wrong, the challenger draws 6 cards.
• **Stacking** – Some groups allow “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four” to be stacked: a player can play a second “Draw Two” on top of a first, forcing the next player to draw 4 (or 8 if stacking continues).
• **No “Draw Four” Challenge** – Some play without the challenge rule for speed. | --- ### Quick Play‑through Example 1. **Deal**: 7 cards each. Flip top card: Red 5. 2. **Player A** (first to play) has a Red 9 → plays it. 3. **Player B** has a Yellow 9 → plays it. 4. **Player C** has a “Skip” → plays it. Player D loses a turn. 5. **Player E** draws a card because they had no playable card. 6. **Player F** has a “Wild” → plays it, chooses Blue. 7. **Player G** has a Blue 2 → plays it. 8. **Player H** has a “Draw Two” → plays it. Player A draws two cards and loses a turn. 9. … and so on until someone goes out. --- ### Tips & Strategy - **Keep a mix of colors** so you’re not stuck when the discard pile changes color. - **Save “Wild Draw Four”** for when you’re about to run out of cards or when you need to block an opponent. - **Watch opponents’ “UNO” calls**; if they forget, you can force them to draw two. - **Use “Reverse” strategically** to change the direction when you’re about to finish or to protect yourself from a “Draw Two.” Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
